prose.intro_html: Chicken bacon ranch usually shows up as a pile of pasta or a stack of tortillas wearing a ranch-flavored disguise, and the carbs do most of the talking. This version cuts them out and lets the good stuff carry the plate. Tender chicken and chopped cauliflower get folded into a real sauce built from cream cheese, heavy cream, and sharp cheddar, seasoned with dry ranch, then baked under one more layer of cheddar and a scatter of bacon until it bubbles. No pasta, no cream-of-something can, no flour. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. That is comfort food that works for your body and your wallet at the same time.
shop_smart: Three pounds of chicken breast is the anchor. Cook it and shred it down to about seven cups of tender meat to fold through the bake. Reach for the big family pack of boneless skinless breasts instead of the little trays, because you are paying for chicken, not packaging. This is where most of the protein and most of the money live.

About two medium heads of cauliflower do the work the pasta used to. Chop them into small pieces, roughly nine cups, and saute them in a little butter until they are crisp-tender so they hold their bite through the bake. They carry the bulk and the fiber without dragging in the carbs a noodle or a cracker topping would.

Cream cheese and heavy cream build the sauce, not a soup can. Grab an eight ounce brick of cream cheese and about a cup and a half of heavy cream and melt them together into a smooth base. This is the step that turns a pile of ingredients into a casserole instead of a dry bake.

Cheddar shows up twice, so buy enough to cover both jobs. You want about four and three quarter cups of shredded cheddar all told, divided, half melted into the sauce and half blanketing the top. Shredded off a block or straight from the bag both work fine; the sharp stuff just pays you back in more flavor.

Dry ranch mix and bacon are the flavor that names the dish. A tablespoon and a half of the dry ranch seasoning does more work than any bottle of dressing, and a generous cup of bacon bits gets stirred through and scattered over the top. Together they are what make it taste like chicken bacon ranch and not just a cheesy bake.
make_it: Weigh your empty baking dish and write the number down. You will need it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which is the only honest way to portion one big bake.

Heat the oven to 350 degrees F and grease a large baking dish. If your chicken is not already cooked, poach or roast it now, then shred or dice it and set it aside. Chop the cauliflower into small, even pieces.
In your largest skillet or pot over medium heat, melt the butter and add the chopped cauliflower. Saute until it turns crisp-tender, about 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then so it cooks evenly.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cream cheese and the heavy cream and stir until the cream cheese melts completely and the sauce is smooth.
Stir in the shredded chicken, half of the cheddar, the dry ranch seasoning, and most of the bacon, holding back a handful of bacon for the top. Fold until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the mixture level in the baking dish. Scatter the remaining cheddar over the top, then finish with the bacon you held back.

Bake at 350 degrees F for about 30 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the casserole is hot and bubbling. Let it rest a few minutes so it firms up, then weigh the dish, subtract the empty weight from Step 1, and divide across 14 containers.
prose.portion_html: Set the baked dish on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the total. Divide that number by 14 and scoop that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a baked, bubbling chicken bacon ranch casserole that eats like the pasta version and skips the carbs. The chicken and the cheese carry it; the cauliflower does the job the noodles used to, for a lot less.

steps: Weigh the empty baking dish and note the number for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, cook and shred the chicken if needed, and chop the cauliflower.
Saute the chopped cauliflower in the butter until crisp-tender.
Turn the heat to low and melt the cream cheese and heavy cream into a smooth sauce.
Stir in the chicken, half the cheddar, the dry ranch, and most of the bacon.
Spread in the dish, top with the remaining cheddar, and finish with the reserved bacon.
Bake at 350 degrees F for about 30 minutes until bubbling, rest, then weigh the dish and divide across 14 containers.
